value: Confirm gate vs key spelling — PR #234 (draft, head 162c4ea, 2026-11-25). A key maps to its filename, so WHICH SPELLINGS REACH AN ENTRY IS THE FILESYSTEM'S RULE, NOT OURS: case on default macOS/Windows; APFS also folds Unicode (U+017F long s for s, the fi ligature, sharp s for ss, NFD for NFC); HFS+, exFAT and FAT fold case and normalization only. A flag matched by exact spelling let the flagged command run unasked under any other spelling that opens its file. THREE APPROACHES, TWO DROPPED after an independent review each — both had passed ~1,950 tests and a mutation check first. (1) Compare flag names with toLowerCase: misses the Unicode folds, and making list MUTATIONS case-insensitive stripped flags from entries that never moved (ops.* vs OPS.* are two namespaces; the same key in the other store). (2) Exact reads — getOne asking realpath, then readdir, what the opened file is called: realpath returns the name it was last GIVEN after a rename onto another spelling (APFS), listings return NFD on HFS+ and exFAT, and exact pre-reads removed the accidental 'already exists' refusal for a write to a fold spelling. Reverted; reads are main's. (3) Current: compare FILES, not names — fs.statSync with bigint, dev:ino of the key's entry path against each flagged key's path, per store dir (src/utils/entryIdentity.ts). Probed on APFS case-insensitive and case-sensitive, HFS+, exFAT, FAT32: 'same file' is true exactly when the spelling opens the stored file, also after a rewrite through the other spelling. RULES THAT HELD UP: asking whether a key is gated is generous (name case aside, or same file); changing the list is exact (a flag is dropped only under the name it is listed as). THE TEST FOR ANY GATE CHANGE: every entry main gates is still gated on the branch after any command — run as a differential over random command sequences with two projects plus the global store; that harness (reviewer scripts fuzz*.mjs, scratch only) found what unit tests and 26 caught mutations did not. OPEN, OWNER'S CALL: (a) a rename that drops the old name's flag can ungate the same key in ANOTHER PROJECT, because flags are by name per store and the global list applies everywhere — found on `rename -G <namespace>`; recommended: a rename only ever adds flags. (b) `confirm set` on a key that is not a stored entry: refuse (current; loud on a typo, lists nothing where main listed a flag) or accept with a warning. Self-review did not catch any of the three rounds of regressions; a reviewer in its own worktree, told to break it, did each time.
